questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted the opportunity to go on exchange again in university since I have done it before and really enjoyed it

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My major has a lot of mandatory courses which means I had to choose a school based on the availability of certain courses and other than that I wanted to go to an English speaking country as I know that would make it easier to find friends and participate in class, etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: BU provides a full website with everything you need to know from the moment you apply through finding housing, registering courses, getting your visa, and arriving in the US

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a 2-day orientation after we arrived

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Some of the orientation is done with freshmen students which means there is also a lot of information which does not pertain to you as an international student

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: BU has dorms (shared bathroom), suites (own bathroom, shared with roomies) and apartments (kitchen and own bathroom, shared with roomies). It's really hard to get a single room so you have to be prepared to have roommates and sometimes you sleep in the same room with them

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: If you live in the dorms you have to get a meal plan. It's quite expensive but I didn't mind as it was a great place to socialise. If you are placed in an apartment or get housing with access to kitchen you don't have to get a full meal plan but can buy one with a few meals a week if you'd like

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Housing is really hit or miss depending the condition of the building, where you get placed on campus, and who your roommates are which is a shame when it is so expensive. I would say it is important to have realistic expectations but don't be afraid to complain if it's really really bad as there is a chance they can rehouse you

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Exchange students get access to registration as the last ones so you should make a list of first picks for your courses as well as backups in case there is not enough seats in the course. If you go on the website there is a planner where you can put in the courses you intend to take and see if they fit into a schedule together. That way you can add all your courses in one go when registration opens but beware there is a max amount of credits!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a step-by-step guide available but I would recommend you take a look around the website as it is not that intuitive

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Yes but not on the first try. I had to email one of my professors about enrolling in his course which he fortunately allowed so if you're really desperate I would recommend reaching out to hear if they can overenroll the class or put you on a waitlist

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't panic if you don't get all your classes at first. Many students drop in and out of classes all the way until the semester starts and then you have two weeks where you can "shop" by going to different classes and feeling them out before your schedule is locked

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level of undergraduate courses are not as high as in UCPH

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot more participation in class which often counts as part of your grade. If you don't feel comfortable speaking in class there is also the option of going to the professor's office hours and talking to them there. Even though the academic level isn't that high there is a lot of work throughout the semester like smaller assignments, quizzes, presentations and midterms so it's important to stay on top of your work

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
PS241 Developmetal Psychology
PS471 Special Topics in Psychopathology
PH248 Existentialism
MB102 Ashtanga Yoga

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved PH248 with Dr. Sheeley and would recommend anyone to check out the courses from the Philosophy Department. I would also recommend checking out the PDP classes where you can try out different sports for free!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You take a lot more Ubers in Boston because even though there is public transportation it isn't always running at night

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and food is the same price or more expensive than Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are 200+ clubs at BU e.g. knitting club, running club, nordic countries club, etc. You can check them out at the club fair called Splash in the beginning of the semester

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
FitTrek offer hiking trips, whale watching, skiing and kayaking throughout the semester for a reasonable price - the tickets are limited so get them sooner rather than later.
Sign up for the student fitness center which has a swimming pool, hot tub, weight room, running track, basketball and volleyball courts, climbing wall and more.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Check out the different neighborhoods and all the cool museums in time, go outside the city to Cape Cod, Cape Ann, Salem, etc., check out sports games with the Celtics/Bruins/Red Sox, take a weekend trip to New York or DC

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I have been on exchange in the US before so it was super easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be harder to strike up conversation with classmates as most Americans don't hang around after class so I would recommend signing up for clubs, sports or trips and trying to make friends who you can then invite out for coffee or a similar activity

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It can be hard to move past small talk to an actual friendship with some Americans but don't be discouraged and keep trying until you meet someone who puts in effort to you as well

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendliness and helpfulness! If you reach out there is almost no limit to what you can do

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Take advantage of the many cheap and free events in town like discounted prices at Red Sox games and the Symphony Hall and free entry to most museums in Boston if you show your BU student ID
2. Don't miss out on career fairs and your professor's office hours if you're looking for academic and professional opportunities like internships or research positions
3. Check out the different dining halls and find your favorite (mine was Fenway), be aware that the food is more processed and can take some time getting used to

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look out for grants and scholarships as Boston is quite expensive and other than that be open and say yes to things! Even if it doesn't seem that interesting to you, you might meet some cool people and make new memories.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be honest it was the community with the other international students which made the experience super special, I learned about all different kinds of cultures and have friends all over the world now

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing my studies and having fun - there are so many things to do in and around Boston so it was hard to stay on top of work at times which is also an important reason why I went on exchange

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I loved Boston as a city and would definitely recommend studying here!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
